edges.mechanism: Caffeine is a competitive adenosine-receptor antagonist that blunts vasodilator-stress hyperemia, causing false-negative perfusion studies.
edges.evidence: Regadenoson label: avoid methylxanthines >=12 h before MPI; caffeine 200/400 mg reduced reversible defects ~60% (RCT, n=207); false-negative dipyridamole-thallium in 6/8 patients; review advises 24 h hold for dipyridamole.

edges.mechanism: Potent CYP1A2 inhibition; caffeine clearance falls ~80-90% and half-life rises from ~5 h to 31-56 h, risking accumulation/intoxication with daily intake.
edges.evidence: Two randomized crossover PK studies in healthy volunteers; pharmacodynamic effects of a single dose not augmented

edges.mechanism: CYP1A2 inhibition; caffeine half-life 5.2 -> 8.2 h, clearance roughly halved.
Ethinylestradiol-containing COCs reduce caffeine clearance by ~54-55%, reversible within 1 month of stopping.
Tobacco-smoke PAHs induce CYP1A2, accelerating clearance of caffeine (and clozapine, theophylline); induction dissipates after quitting so caffeine exposure rises at the same intake.
Caffeine, a CYP1A2 substrate/inhibitor, can raise plasma clozapine levels; smoking lowers them.
edges.evidence: Review of PK interactions (case reports and trials)

edges.mechanism: Caffeine increases renal lithium clearance; stopping caffeine raised serum lithium and worsened tremor.

Overlapping methylxanthine with additive caffeine-like adverse effects; caffeine and theophylline are interconverted metabolites, both CYP1A2-dependent; caffeine metabolites can falsely raise some office theophylline assays.
High-dose caffeine with tranylcypromine/phenelzine linked to hypertension; generally manageable with monitoring.
Additive pressor and chronotropic effects: dextroamphetamine raises BP 2-4 mm Hg and HR 3-6 bpm; caffeine acutely raises BP (~8/6 mm Hg). Mechanistic inference; no combination trial found.
edges.evidence: Drug label plus MA of caffeine BP trials; inference

edges.mechanism: Sympathomimetic plus methylxanthine; ephedra banned in US 2004 after cardiovascular reports.
edges.evidence: Danish registry (257,364 users) found no substantially increased CV event risk with prescribed ephedrine/caffeine (adjusted OR 0.95)

edges.mechanism: Combination improves attention-switching accuracy and alertness beyond placebo.
edges.evidence: MA of RCTs (SMD 0.33 attention switching) plus RCT

edges.mechanism: Acute caffeine after creatine loading retains its benefit, but chronic caffeine during creatine loading may blunt creatine's effect (opposing effects on muscle relaxation time, GI distress).
Combined caffeine + taurine credibly better than either alone for anaerobic capacity and reaction time.
Combination produced the largest jump-height gains and lowest RPE.
Green tea preparations contain caffeine as well as catechins; stacking increases total caffeine dose (inference).
Shared CYP1A2 metabolism: 200 mg evening caffeine increased nocturnal melatonin AUC by 32%; caffeine also impairs sleep.
Caffeine increases urinary magnesium and calcium excretion; net 24-h losses 0.16 mmol Mg and 0.32 mmol Ca.

Coffee/tea polyphenols inhibit non-heme iron absorption (coffee with meal -39%); effect is from polyphenols, not caffeine; no study of heme-iron supplements with coffee found. Separating coffee from iron-containing meals by >=1 h before avoids inhibition.
Observational dose-response associations with pregnancy loss and low birth weight; MR does not support causality. EFSA and ACOG: <=200 mg/day.
edges.evidence: Dose-response MAs, MR study, EFSA opinion, ACOG committee opinion

edges.mechanism: Adenosine antagonism is anxiogenic; 400-750 mg challenges triggered panic attacks in ~51-54% of panic-disorder patients vs 1.7% of controls.
Caffeine reduces total sleep time (~35-45 min), sleep efficiency and slow-wave sleep and prolongs sleep onset; 400 mg disrupts sleep within 12 h of bedtime.
edges.evidence: Two MAs of crossover trials and a dose-timing RCT

edges.mechanism: Acute pressor response (+8.1/+5.7 mm Hg for >=3 h) in hypertensive people, but no long-term BP rise or excess CVD risk with habitual coffee.
edges.evidence: MA of trials and cohorts; MR

edges.mechanism: Slow CYP1A2 metabolizers: coffee associated with higher nonfatal MI risk (OR 1.64 at >=4 cups/d) and impaired cycling performance at 4 mg/kg in CC genotype.
edges.evidence: Case-control study (2,014 cases) and RCT (n=101); not validated prospectively

edges.mechanism: Easy to measure lethal doses; ~1,200 mg rapidly can cause seizures; deaths involve tablets/powder, not beverages.
edges.evidence: FDA guidance (2018) and consumer update; forensic reviews
